what: The Direction B sheets declare 46 distinct font-size values: 21 fixed px sizes (10 of them between 12 and 17px at 0.5px steps: 12, 12.5, 13, 13.5, 14, 14.5, 15, 15.5, 16, 17), 17 rem sizes (Clocker only), 4 clamps. With them: 36 line-heights, 74 size/line-height pairs and 67 size/line-height/weight triples. 13px (32 declarations) and 15px (66) belong to no DESIGN.MD role. The five type-role tokens in b-tokens.css are read 4 times in about 520 font-size declarations.
why: Ten sizes inside a 5px band cannot be told apart, so hierarchy has to come from weight and colour alone and every page drifts by half a pixel from the next. DESIGN.MD (B1) already names the roles; the code has not adopted them.
fix: Adopt 8 roles as tokens and write sizes only through them: display 30/36 700 -0.02em (Home 34/40, pushed page 28/34), figure 24/30 600 -0.02em tabular, title 20/26 700 -0.01em, title-sm 17/22 700 -0.01em, body 15.5/22, body-sm 14.5/20, meta 13.5/18, caption 12.5/16. Locked component sizes that stay: count 12/700, tab label 10.5/13 500, inputs and the select 16px, segment label 14/600, band sub-line 14px, state-card title 16/22 600 (all fixed in DESIGN.MD). Fold: 13 -> meta 13.5/18; 15 on buttons and menu items -> body-sm 14.5/20, 15 on reading lines -> body 15.5/22; 12 that is not a count -> caption 12.5/16; 18 and 22 -> title 20/26; 26 and 32 -> figure 24/30 or display 30/36; 40 -> Home 34/40. Asking Jose whether 14 and 16 (non-input) may fold into 14.5 and 15.5 would remove the last two half-step neighbours.

what: Line-heights do not follow the roles: 19px is used 30 times and 21px 33 times where the roles say 18, 20 or 22 (row titles are 15.5/21 in 8 rules; the role is 15.5/22). 36 distinct line-height values in total, 21 of them in px and 14 unitless. Weights: 600 (179), 700 (114), 500 (27), 400 (7). Letter-spacing has 19 spellings of 14 values (-0.005em to -0.05em, 0.01em to 0.08em).
why: A 1px line-height difference moves every baseline in a list, so two cards with the same rows end at different heights. Six negative tracking values on titles of the same size read as inconsistent optical weight.
fix: Line-height comes with the role (16, 18, 20, 22, 26, 30, 36, 40): 19 -> 18 (meta) or 20 (body-sm); 21 -> 22 (body). Weights: 400 text, 600 labels, row titles and buttons, 700 titles, values and counts; keep 500 only for the 10.5px tab label and a chosen menu item. Letter-spacing: -0.02em at 24px and up, -0.01em at 17 to 20px, 0 below, 0.05em on uppercase eyebrows; delete -0.005, -0.015, -0.025, -0.03, -0.035, -0.04, -0.05, 0.01, 0.02, 0.04, 0.08.

what: Checked and sound: tabular-nums is set on 22 number selectors (figures, row values, counts, pills, td, time, Clocker clock and keys) with proportional figures elsewhere; text-wrap is balance 31 times and pretty 31 times; no letter-spacing in px; no weight under 400; no font-feature-settings. Gaps: -webkit-font-smoothing is set inside two component sheets instead of the root; every size and line-height is in px, so a browser font-size preference does not scale the app (zoom still works); single-line truncation (ellipsis, 10 rules) has no visible way to the full text in CSS.
why: These are the cheap details that separate a finished product from a styled one; the px convention is a project choice recorded in DESIGN.MD, so it is noted, not a defect.
fix: Move font smoothing to the root rule. Keep the px pairs (DESIGN.MD writes roles as 12.5/16). For each ellipsis rule confirm the row opens a detail view or carries a title; where it does not, let the text wrap with text-wrap: pretty.

what: 47 distinct px values across 1,641 padding, margin and gap uses; 60% sit on a 4px grid (2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24...). Off-grid: 18px (208 uses), 22px (154), 14px (129), 10px (98), then 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 3 and 1px (45 together) and 26, 30, 34, 38, 42, 66, 70, 81, 218, 222. As horizontal insets 14, 18 and 22 are DESIGN.MD values (phone gutter 14, phone row inset 18, desktop row inset 22): about 304 uses. The other about 172 uses of 14/18/22 are gaps, vertical padding and margins, and 10px is used 78 times as a gap or vertical step.
why: Three approved insets are fine as named values; the same numbers reused as gaps and vertical padding are what make cards feel hand-tuned: 10, 12 and 14 appear side by side as the gap in the same kind of row.
fix: Scale: 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64 (6 only inside chips and count pills). Three named insets outside the grid, horizontal only: --b-gutter 14px (phone page edge), --b-inset 18px (phone card and row sides), --b-inset-wide 22px (tablet and desktop card and row sides). Fold everything else: 10 -> 8 or 12; 14 as gap or vertical -> 12 or 16; 18 as gap or vertical -> 16 or 20; 22 as gap or vertical -> 20 or 24; 5/7 -> 4 or 8; 9/11 -> 8 or 12; 13 -> 12; 26 -> 24; 30/34 -> 32; 38/42 -> 40; 66/70 -> 64 or 72. A later decision for Jose: 16/16/24 insets would put the whole system on one grid.

what: The standard measures exist only as repeated literals, and two differ by layer: card header min-height is 44px in the kit, 46px on Employee phones (DESIGN.MD says 46) and 52px on Employee desktop; the cards' bottom padding is 22px on phones and 24px on desktop; a c-row is 60px with 10px 22px padding and a 14px gap on desktop while a b-row is 64px with 12px 18px and a 12px gap.
why: Without tokens for card padding, row height, section gap and gutter, each new page re-derives them, which is how 44/46/52 happened.
fix: Tokens: --b-row-h 64px (two lines), --b-row-h-1 56px (one line), --b-row-gap 12px, --b-row-py 12px, --b-card-head-h 46px, --b-card-gap 12px phone / 20px wide, --b-band-gap 24px, --b-lift 40px phone / 52px wide, --b-page-x 14px phone / 24px tablet / 40px desktop, --b-page-bottom 24px (phone 22 -> 24). Reading column 812px (B6; owner-b-desktop.css still has 860px four times).

what: Outside b-tokens.css the B sheets hold 73 distinct hex literals (565 uses) and 67 distinct rgb()/rgba() literals (264 uses). 396 literal uses equal a --b-* token value (265 are #FFFFFF; auth-b.css alone has 125), against DESIGN.MD F3 ("a colour literal that equals a --b-* value is written as the token"). 51 hexes match no token; the most used is #0B3B38 (28 uses: the ink of white pills on the band). 44 more hex values are local custom-property copies (owner-b.css 14, clocker.module.css 25).
why: Every literal is a place the palette can drift, and several already have: the same amber dot is #E9A23B, #E2A13B and #FFC46B.
fix: Add the missing roles to b-tokens.css and replace literals: --b-on-white-pill #0B3B38 (ink on a white pill over the band), --b-red-strong #8F1C13 (red hover/pressed, 5 uses), --b-amber-solid #E9A23B (rings, bars, dots on white; folds #E2A13B), --b-amber-on-band #FFC46B (folds #FFD596), --b-green-on-band #7EF0C7 (folds #9BF0D6, #6FE0CF, #A8F0E4), --b-green-solid #2FB37F (folds #1D8A55), --b-ink-surface #17302D (folds #152A28, #11221F), --b-band-end #08504C (folds #08524E, #0B4F4B, #06403C). Then #FFFFFF -> a new --b-surface on backgrounds and var(--b-on-band) on text; remove the duplicate token block in owner-b.css and point the Clocker's --ck-* at --b-*.

what: The neutral ladder has 29 values where the tokens define 9. Between L 0.89 and 0.99 there are 17 fills that differ by one or two steps per channel: #E1E5E6, #E3E6E7, #E3E7E8, #E4E8E8, #E6E9EA, #E6EBEA, #EBEEEE, #ECEEEF, #EDF0F0, #EEF1F1, #F0F2F3, #F2F5F4, #F4F6F6, #F4F7F6, #F7F8F8, #F7F9F9, #FBFCFC. Mid greys: #7A8489, #7D868B, #8A9399, #8C9397, #9AA3A8, #A3A9AE, #A7ACB1, #B5BBBF, #D3D9DB, #D5DADC. Pure #000000 appears 7 times (mask gradients).
why: Near-identical greys are invisible one at a time and visible together: a hairline at #E4E8E8 beside one at #ECEEEF, a track at #EDF0F0 beside a chip at #F0F2F3.
fix: Seven neutrals: ink #111517, ink2 #3F464B, grey #6A7176 (text on white), grey-on-fill #5E666B, field-edge #8C9397, line #ECEEEF, quiet #F0F2F3; plus canvas #F2F5F4, hover #F7F9F9 and one new pressed step --b-press #E6EBEA. Fold: #E1E5E6, #E3E6E7, #E3E7E8, #E4E8E8, #E6E9EA, #EBEEEE -> line; #EDF0F0, #EEF1F1, #F4F6F6, #F4F7F6 -> quiet; #F7F8F8, #FBFCFC -> hover; #7A8489, #7D868B, #8A9399, #9AA3A8 -> field-edge; #D3D9DB, #D5DADC -> line (decorative) or field-edge (a field or switch edge that must reach 3:1); #A3A9AE, #A7ACB1, #B5BBBF -> one --b-icon-faint (see SY-008).

what: Measured pairs (WCAG 2 ratio). Pass: ink/white 18.37; ink2/white 9.59; grey #6A7176/white 4.96; grey-on-fill #5E666B on quiet 5.21, on teal-50 5.16; teal/white 6.09, teal/teal-50 5.37; amber #8A4B00/amber-50 6.19; red #B42318/red-50 5.75; green #1D6B45/green-50 5.72; white on the band 5.77 (lightest stop) to 9.28; white .86 on the solid band 4.71; white on glass over the lightest stop 4.52; field edge #8C9397/white 3.12. Below threshold: grey #6A7176 on canvas 4.52 (at the line), on quiet 4.41, on teal-50 4.37, on line 4.26; white .86 on glass 3.80; field edge on canvas 2.84; row chevron #B5BBBF/white 1.94; amber solid #E9A23B/white 2.17 and #E2A13B 2.24; green ring #2FB37F/white 2.67; coral dot #FF6B5E on the band 2.07; #FFC46B on the band 3.67. No rule sets grey text and a tinted fill together, so the grey-on-fill misses could not be located from CSS: Not verified in a browser.
why: The token set is right; the risk is --b-grey (106 uses) inherited into chips, quiet pills and tinted rows where --b-grey-on-fill (3 uses) was meant, and graphics that carry state below 3:1.
fix: Set color: var(--b-grey-on-fill) on every grey chip, quiet pill, count on a fill, and text inside .b-ico--grey; sub-lines inside glass use --b-on-band, never --b-on-band-2 (DESIGN.MD already says so). Chevrons that mean "this row opens" use --b-field-edge #8C9397 (3.12). Amber and green rings keep their word or glyph (they do today) and gain a 3:1 edge only where they stand alone. Give the coral dot a 2px ring in the surface colour under it so it separates by shape. Fields drawn on the canvas use a white fill.

what: 28 distinct border-radius values. In use: 22px (78), 999px (59), 0 (45), 14px (44), 16px (29), 18px (27), 21px (21), 20px (19), 4px (14), 50% (12), 10px (11), 12px (11), 11px (9), 24px (9), 3px (8), 8px (6), then 2, 5, 6, 7, 9, 13, 15, 17, 19, 23, 26. 61 declarations write a pill as half its height (16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 26px). The tokens are barely read: 22px is a literal 73 times against 3 uses of --b-radius-card; 999px a literal 32 times.
why: DESIGN.MD says every button, chip and segment thumb is a pill (999px). Half-height radii only stay pills while the height stays the same; the day a 42px button becomes 48px its 21px corners stop being a pill.
fix: Four radii and one approved exception: --b-radius-pill 999px (buttons, chips, segments, circles, thin bars; folds 50%, 3px bars and every half-height value), --b-radius-card 22px (cards, sheets, finder, ink tile, state cards; folds 20, 23, 24, 26 and the 18/20px glass strip), --b-radius-field 14px (fields, selects, search, inner tiles; folds 13, 15, 16 where it is not a menu), new --b-radius-sm 10px (day cells, schedule blocks, menu items, focus rounding; folds 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12). The menu popover keeps DESIGN.MD's 16px.

what: Concentric radius check (outer = inner + padding). Sound: the segmented control (pill track, 4px in, pill thumb), the ink tile with its pill button, cards whose rows run edge to edge. Off: the tablet and desktop menu is 16px with 6px padding and 8px items (16 = 10 + 6, so the items are 2px too tight); the glass figure strip is 18px on phones and 20px on desktop for the same component; fields at 14px inside a 22px card with an 18px inset are separate surfaces (padding under 24px, so strictly 4px, judged by eye and fine).
why: A mismatched inner corner is the first thing the eye reads as "not quite finished" on menus, which open on every page.
fix: Menu items 10px (--b-radius-sm), popover 16px, 6px in. One radius for the glass strip: --b-radius-card. DESIGN.MD (F3) states 8px items: update it with the code.

what: 90 distinct box-shadow values besides none (260 uses). True elevations are few but written many ways: the card shadow is a literal 25 times, var(--nvd-card) 19 times and var(--b-elev-1) 6 times; --b-elev-2 is read twice. 25 shadows use black (0 8px 18px -8px rgb(0 0 0 / .45) 14 times on white pills over the band, 0 2px 6px rgb(0 0 0 / .18) 7 times) and others rgb(16 24 32), rgb(6 30 28), rgb(5 30 28), although DESIGN.MD fixes one shadow colour, rgb(16 40 38). Seven more card-like recipes exist once or twice (auth-b.css:101, 114, 311; owner-b.css:284; account.css:121; employee-b-desktop.css:651; owner-b-desktop.css:31). The rest are rings and hairlines drawn with box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px white .16 (28) and .18 (7), inset 0 1px 0 #ECEEEF (25), inset 1px/2px field and state rings.
why: Three elevations only read as a ramp when every surface uses exactly them; seven near-copies flatten the ramp, and black shadows on the band look heavier than the teal-tinted ones beside them.
fix: Keep --b-elev-1 (cards), --b-elev-2 (sheets, menus, popovers, finder), --b-elev-glow (the one teal primary). Add --b-elev-band: 0 8px 18px -8px rgb(16 40 38 / .5) for white pills on the band and replace all black shadows with it. Name the rings: --b-ring-glass: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--b-glass-edge) (folds .18 into .16), --b-divider: inset 0 1px 0 var(--b-line), --b-ring-field: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--b-field-edge), --b-ring-on: inset 0 0 0 2px var(--b-teal), --b-ring-error: inset 0 0 0 2px var(--b-red) (folds the 1.5px rings). Point --nvd-card at --b-elev-1. Cards already keep border: 1px solid transparent for forced-colors (owner-b.css:156); do the same wherever a ring is the only edge.

what: 574 Phosphor icon elements in the app (tests and ui-preview excluded). Weight: 265 bold, 291 with no weight prop (so they draw Phosphor regular) in 99 files, 7 fill, 7 duotone, 4 regular. The Direction B components are consistent (73 of 74 bold; the exception is owner-b/team-b.tsx); the legacy components that B restyles are not: communication-compose.tsx (23 unweighted), communication-detail.tsx (16), reports.tsx (13), employee-mobile/pay.tsx (13), calendar-subscription-panel.tsx (9), employee-time-panel.tsx (9), notification-inbox.tsx (9), employee-shift-sheet.tsx (7), payroll/payroll-ui.tsx (7). Sizes: 17 distinct size props (18: 128, 20: 80, 16: 38, 22: 25, 24: 17, 28: 13, then 10, 11, 13, 14, 15, 17, 19, 23, 25, 26, 30) and 243 icons sized by CSS (svg rules at 22, 18, 16, 20, 15, 21, 10px).
why: DESIGN.MD fixes Phosphor bold. A bold icon draws a 1.7px stroke at 18px and a regular one 1.1px; next to 600-weight row titles the regular ones look thin and unfinished, and the two weights meet on the same page (a B card above a legacy panel).
fix: One weight: bold everywhere, fill only for the current tab, no duotone or regular. The icons are imported from dist/ssr, which does not read IconContext, so add weight="bold" at each call site (or one small wrapper) and a lint rule. One size per context: 16px inline with meta or caption text, in chips and as field affordances (caret, lock); 18px for a row's leading glyph in its 36px circle, the row chevron and icons inside buttons; 20px for band controls (back, close, bell), menu items and the 40px glass circle; 22px for the tab bar, sidebar, rail and the 48px state circle. Fold 13/14/15 -> 16, 17/19 -> 18, 23/24/25/26 -> 22 (or 20 in a control), 28/30 -> 22 inside a 48px circle.

what: Icon circles come in six sizes: 28px (finder kinds), 32px (.b-add), 36px (row lead, route note), 40px (glass back and bell), 44px (.b-ib) and 48px (state card), with glyphs of 14 to 22px.
why: Six circle sizes for four jobs; 32 and 36 sit in the same lists.
fix: Four circles, glyph at about half: 28/16 (dense pickers), 36/18 (rows), 40/20 (glass controls on the band, 44px hit area), 48/22 (state cards). Fold 32 -> 36 and draw .b-ib at 40 with a 44px hit area.

what: Five button families render under Direction B: b-btn (83 class uses in TSX), c-btn (320), q-btn (234), q-bs (29) and nv-btn (105), plus wc-btn and sig-btn. In the B sheets they are set to 10 heights (32, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 48, 52, 56px), 9 radii (16, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22, 24, 26, 999px) and 7 label sizes (13.5, 14, 14.5, 15, 15.5, 16, 17px), with 600 and 700 both used for the same variant. The kit's own base is 36px/14px/600 (owner-b.css:143), its full-width form is 52px/16px on phones and 48px/15.5 on desktop, the white band pill is 40px on phones and 48px on desktop.
why: A person meets a 36px, a 40px, a 42px and a 44px pill doing the same job on four pages. This is the most visible gap to Gusto or Homebase, whose buttons come in three sizes.
fix: One set, all pills (--b-radius-pill), label 600: lg 48px, 0 24px, 15.5/22 (form footer, band action, full-width primary); md 40px drawn with a 44px hit area (44px drawn on coarse pointers, as DESIGN.MD requires for decision pairs), 0 16px, 14.5/20, min-width 96px in rows; sm 32px drawn with a 44px hit area, 0 12px, 13.5/18 (dense rows only). Variants: primary (teal, white text, --b-elev-glow at lg only, one per screen), secondary (teal-50, teal text; today's ghost), quiet (--b-quiet, ink), danger (red, white text; in rows red text on red-50), text (teal 600, no fill, 44px target); on the band: white (ink #0B3B38, --b-elev-band) and glass. Disabled: the one pair. 56px stays for the Clocker only. Fold 34 -> 32; 36, 38, 42 -> 40; 52 -> 48; 13.5/14/15 labels per size above.

what: Legacy buttons that still differ visibly under B (read from the cascade; Not verified in a browser). (1) nv-btn has no Direction B rule at all: under data-nv-corp it is an 8px-corner, 44px rectangle (corp-quiet-bridge.css:124), 12px/52px in the kit, pressing to scale .98 over 90ms linear; it renders in reports, time-off review, calendar subscription, update detail, wave-b forms, passkeys, route errors and PendingButton. (2) On phones owner-b-pages.css:134 makes only primary c-btn and q-btn pills; c-btn--secondary, --neutral, --danger keep the corporate 8px corners with a 1px ring and q-btn--sec / --quiet keep 12px. (3) q-bs is 32px/16px in Quiet, 36px on the Employee schedule, 38 or 40px on desktop and 44px in decision pairs. (4) auth-b.css draws 52px buttons with 26px corners and its own shadow.
why: DESIGN.MD B1: "every button, chip and segment thumb on B surfaces is a pill". A rectangle with 8px corners beside a pill is the clearest "old screen" signal left in the app.
fix: Add nv-btn to the shared B button rule (b-foundation.css:179-181 and owner-b-desktop.css:146) with the SY-014 sizes, or render BButton from PendingButton and RouteError. Drop the :not(--secondary/--neutral/--danger/--sec/--quiet) exclusions at owner-b-pages.css:134 and give those the secondary or quiet variant. Map q-bs to size sm (md in decision pairs). Auth: 48px lg pill, --b-radius-pill, --b-elev-glow.

what: Three row patterns under B. b-row (kit): min-height 64px, padding 12px 18px, gap 12px, 36px lead, title 15.5/21 600, sub 13.5/18 grey, value 15.5/20 700, 18px bold chevron in #B5BBBF. c-row (corporate): 60px base with 8px 16px; under B on desktop 60px, 10px 22px, gap 14px, title 15.5 or 15px/21 600, value 14px 600 or 700; 56px with 10px 14px on Employee Time. q-row (Quiet): 64px base with 0 20px; 60px on B desktop, 52px on some phone pages. Sub-lines are 18px tall in the kit and 19px on desktop; Employee desktop fields set both title and sub to 15px.
why: Lists are most of this product. Rows of 52, 56, 60 and 64px with 12 or 14px gaps make two cards on one page look like two apps.
fix: One row: min-height 64px with a sub-line, 56px without; padding 12px var(--b-inset) (18px phone, 22px wide); gap 12px; lead 36px circle or avatar (18px glyph); title body 15.5/22 600 ink, text-wrap pretty; sub meta 13.5/18 grey; trailing value body 15.5/22 700 tabular, or one md/sm button, or a chip; chevron CaretRight 18px bold in --b-field-edge only when the row navigates; one inset divider (--b-divider) starting at the text edge; hover --b-hover inside (hover: hover); pressed --b-press with no scale. Dense tables (Timecards 52px) stay as DESIGN.MD records.

what: Chips are 22px (rows), 24px (card headers and desktop) and 30px (Employee Pay), with 7, 8, 9 or 12px side padding, 12, 12.5 or 13.5px text and radii written as 999px, 11px, 12px and 15px. Count pills are 22px and 24px at 12.5/700 while the count role is 12/700.
why: Small, but chips sit beside every title.
fix: Chip: 22px in rows, 24px in card headers (both DESIGN.MD), 0 8px, caption 12.5/16 600, pill. Count pill: 20px, 0 6px, 12/700 (the segmented control's token). Fold 30px/13.5 to the 24px chip.

what: The press scale ignores reduced motion on most buttons. b-foundation.css:180 sets :active { scale: var(--b-press-scale) } on .b-btn, .c-btn, .q-btn, .q-bs and .wc-btn outside any prefers-reduced-motion query; the kit gates the same press correctly at owner-b.css:344-345 and time.css:193, and corp.css:232 / quiet.css:147 turn the transition off, but the foundation rule is more specific and loads last. DESIGN.MD B1: "press is scale .96 over 150ms ease-out (none under reduced motion)".
why: Motion that ignores the reduced-motion preference is an accessibility failure (better-ui and better-accessibility both rank it High), and it contradicts an approved rule.
fix: Wrap the scale declaration at b-foundation.css:180 in @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) and keep the background-color change as the static cue. Do the same for nv-btn when it joins the rule.

what: Motion is sparse and mostly correct: 33 transition declarations (23 at 150ms ease-out) and 24 animation declarations in 9,422; no transition: all; no will-change; press is .96 in all six :active rules; hover is inside (hover: hover) for 25 declarations; the entrance is 300ms ease-out with 100ms stagger, 4px blur and 12px rise, with a 200ms fade under reduced motion; the inspector leaves in 150ms over 12px. Deviations from the exact values: the Clocker transitions transform over 120ms and backgrounds over 90, 120 and 140ms with the default ease (clocker.module.css:183, 211, 234, 245, 284); auth carets rotate over 160ms (auth-b.css:246, 401); a reduced-motion fade is 160ms ease-out where the others are 200ms linear (requests.css:154); three hover rules in auth-b.css are outside (hover: hover) (171, 237, 325); legacy presses still exist at .98 (kit.css:245 nv-btn, corp.css:117), .97 (quiet.css:118), .985 and .99. 15 distinct durations in all (90, 100, 120, 140, 150, 160, 200, 220, 300, 320, 420, 800, 900, 1300, 8000ms) and 6 easings; 150ms is a literal 20 times against 2 uses of --b-dur-press.
why: Two press speeds and two easings are felt, not seen: the Clocker's buttons answer faster and less smoothly than the app's.
fix: Tokens: --b-dur-fast 150ms (press, hover, colour, caret rotate, exits), --b-dur-enter 300ms, --b-dur-fade 200ms (reduced-motion cross-fade), --b-stagger 100ms, --b-ease-out ease-out, --b-ease-spin linear, --b-press-scale .96, --b-enter-rise 12px, --b-enter-blur 4px. Clocker: scale, background-color 150ms ease-out (keys may stay at 90ms for background only: a keystroke is high-frequency). Auth carets 150ms. Wrap auth-b.css:171, 237, 325 in (hover: hover). Replace 150ms literals with the token.

what: Micro-interactions that are missing or uneven in the B layers. Sheets and menus: only the desktop inspector has an exit (b-foundation.css:385); no B rule gives a phone bottom sheet, a menu popover or the finder an enter or exit, and overscroll-behavior: contain appears once in the B sheets (the Clocker). Rows: pressed feedback is rgb(16 24 32 / .04) on b-row only (owner-b.css:179); c-row and q-row have none in B. Toggles and the segmented thumb: no B transition (the legacy c-switch has its own). Success: the Clocker has a drawn check (320ms pop, 420ms draw); the app's own moments (timecard approved, schedule published, request sent) have no shared treatment in B. Skeletons are static #ECEEEF bars.
why: Premium products feel finished because the rare moments (a sheet arriving, a success) are choreographed while routine taps stay instant. Today the rare moments are instant too.
fix: Sheet and popover enter: opacity 0 to 1, translateY 12px to 0 (bottom sheet: from its own height), 300ms ease-out; exit 150ms ease-out, opacity and -12px; reduced motion: 200ms opacity only; add overscroll-behavior: contain to every scrollable sheet, menu and the finder. Rows: background --b-press on :active, 150ms, no scale. Switch thumb and segmented thumb: translate 150ms ease-out, none under reduced motion (tab switches stay instant otherwise). Success: one pattern, a 48px green circle whose check cross-fades in (scale .25 to 1, opacity, 4px blur, 300ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)), with the words as the static cue. Skeleton: keep static, or an opacity pulse of 1 to .6 over 1300ms under no-preference; never a moving gradient.

what: DESIGN.MD B1: "disabled is #F0F2F3 with #8C9397 text, no opacity fades". Opacity is still the disabled look in the Clocker (.55 at clocker.module.css:188, 199, 289; .45 on keys at 249; .88 busy at 206), on Employee inline buttons (requests.css:116, .55) and on the weekly confirmation (schedule.css:56, .55). Past days fade at .55 and .6 (employee-b.css:114, schedule.css:44), and counts fade at .7, .72 and .86.
why: Two disabled looks in one product; an opacity fade over the band or a tint also lowers contrast unpredictably.
fix: Use --b-disabled-bg and --b-disabled-ink for every disabled control and remove the opacity. For past days use --b-grey text instead of opacity; for counts use the count pill.

what: At least nine state patterns render. Direction B: BState (21 uses in 15 files) and BLoadingScreen (through RouteSkeleton in 29 of 44 loading.tsx files). Older: SettingsLoading / RecoveryLoading / SettingsRouteLoading with wc-skeleton bars in nv-card (13 loading.tsx files under settings); EmptyState (.nevora-empty, 25 uses in 11 files: locations, breaks, Clocker settings, positions, manager inbox, weekly roster); c-empty (59 uses in 17 files: reports, who's working, team overview, payroll runs and statements, my pay, hours, notifications, time off, requests page); q-empty (39 uses in 19 files: reports, availability team list, time off, update detail, manager inbox, my schedule, swaps, shift requests, time panel, notifications, updates, company policies, scheduling rules); c-note (79 uses in 28 files) as the catch-all inline note; c-error (52), q-error (15), wb-error (13), wb-notice (11), wb-note (38) for errors and notices; RouteError with nv-btn in five error.tsx files; two error.tsx files with their own markup (app/app/error.tsx, app/app/employees/error.tsx). The B sheets restyle some of these classes (owner-b-pages.css 13 rules, owner-b-desktop.css 14) but q-empty and c-empty remain a grey sentence with no icon, title or action.
why: DESIGN.MD B2 and B5: one state card (48px icon circle, 16/22 title, one line, one teal pill, left-aligned) for failed, offline, paused, locked, loading and empty. A bare grey line is where an app looks unfinished, and it gives the person nothing to do next.
fix: Move every empty and failed state to BState: kind="empty" with the page's glyph, a title, one line and, where one exists, the action. Order of work by reach: q-empty (19 files), c-empty (17), EmptyState (11; keep the component name, render BState inside), RouteError (5 routes). Settings loading screens: draw BLoadingScreen inside SettingsFrame so the band and the two 22px cards match the other 29 routes. Inline form errors: one class (red-50 note, 36px red circle, body-sm text) replacing c-error, q-error and wb-error. c-note stays for quiet 13.5/18 helper lines only.

what: The kit's "empty" kind defaults to a WarningCircle glyph (b-kit.tsx:201), so an empty list that passes no icon shows a warning. Skeleton bars are 14px tall with 7px corners in B (employee-b.css:221) and 13px with 4px corners in the corporate skeleton (corp.css:447). The state card's padding is 16px with a 14px gap where cards use 18px.
why: An empty list is not a warning; small mismatches between the two skeletons show when a route swaps one for the other.
fix: Default the empty kind to a neutral glyph (Tray or the page's own) and require icon for kind="empty". Skeleton bar: 12px tall, pill, --b-line, 12px apart, in a card with the standard inset. State card: padding var(--b-inset), gap 12px.

what: b-tokens.css defines the system, but the sheets mostly bypass it: type roles 4 uses; --b-radius-card 3 (22px literal 73); --b-radius-pill 5 outside the segment tokens (999px literal 32); --b-radius-field 3 (14px literal 39); --b-elev-1 6 (literal 25, --nvd-card 19); --b-dur-press 2 (150ms literal 20); the focus pair 3 (2px solid var(--b-teal) / #0B6E69 / #FFFFFF / #fff written out 37 times). owner-b.css keeps a second copy of the palette and the Clocker a third (--ck-*, 25 hex definitions). Direction B rules also live in 25 of 169 stylesheets, and 4,950 of 9,422 declarations in the audited set are !important.
why: A token that is not read is documentation. The next palette or radius change will need 70 edits instead of one, and will miss some.
fix: One pass per token family, each provable with the existing computed-style comparison because values do not change: replace literals that equal a token with the token; delete the palette copy in owner-b.css; alias --ck-* to --b-*. Add the tokens proposed in review-system.md (type roles as font shorthands, spacing, radius-sm, elev-band, rings, motion, row and button sizes) before the visual folding starts.
